title: Moules Marinières
summary: A classic French dish of mussels steamed in white wine with garlic and parsley. Briny, aromatic, and best served with bread for soaking up the sauce.
steps: Rinse the mussels under cold water, scrubbing the shells well. Discard any with broken shells, and tap open mussels that stay open; throw away any that do not close.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a large, lidded pot over medium heat. Add the shallot and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until softened but not browned.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine and bring it to a lively simmer.
Add the mussels, cover tightly, and cook for 4 to 6 minutes, shaking the pot once or twice, until most shells have opened.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the parsley, black pepper, salt, and lemon juice.
Ladle the mussels and broth into warm bowls. Serve immediately with crusty bread if desired.
